the type of the argument is `unsigned long` which [maps](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long) to uint32. Is that a thing on Fuzzilli? Also could we match uint32's bounds?

Mutators will mutate this to any Int64 value [[1]]. I don't really think it's too important to add support for a LoadUInt32 operation so that Fuzzilli's mutators can be more intelligent. Do you think it's something for the backlog?

if it's an echo, shouldn't the timestamp be the same?

The same timestamp doesn't get plumbed through with the echo. The timestamp given by `clipDescription.getTimestamp()` is what was recorded at this point: 

`CommitToAndroidClipboard` --> `Java_Clipboard_setClipboardText` --> `ClipboardImpl.setClipboardText` --> `setPrimaryClipNoException` --> `setPrimaryClip` -->  `mClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip`, in which Android sets the `ClipDesription`'s timestamp to the current time.

Then **later** at the end of the same `CommitToAndroidClipboard` call, we record  `ClipboardMap::UpdateLastModifiedTime`. This is what the `getLastModifiedTimeMs()` uses in `onPrimaryClipChanged`. 

So some wall-clock time might have elapsed between those two timestamps …

When would `IsEmpty()` be true? Is it ONLY in the case where we exercise `optional` and the bindings layer passes in *no* `ScriptValue` object, so we construct a default one? If so, and if that's the only point of `optional` in the IDL and we still have to handle it ourselves, then we might as well get rid of `optional` and let the bindings layer automatically pass in a default-constructed `ScriptValue` that we check here anyways. Is that posisble to do?

If inputObject is not `optional`, calling `modelContext.executeTool(tool)` in JS with 1 argument fails synchronously with:
```
TypeError: Failed to execute 'executeTool' on 'ModelContext': 2 arguments required, but only 1 present.
```

The C++ implementation is not even be called.

I see. In that case, why don't we just use `optional any inputObject = {}`? Is this possible? I'm just trying to simplify things by not having us need to distinguish between "empty" and "undefined", if we want both to fallback to `= {}` default object behavior.

I see per https://chromium-review.git.corp.google.com/c/chromium/src/+/8250826/comment/203cb0b7_8570dbcb/ we originally thought that `= {}` could not be used for `optional any` values, since Web IDL states

> Optional argument default values can also be specified using the two token value {}, which represents a default-initialized (as if from ES null or an object with no properties) dictionary value. The type of this value is the same as the type of the optional argument it is being used as the default value of. That type must be a dictionary type, or a union type that has a dictionary type in its flattened member types.

And we thought that `any` didn't include "dictionary types" in its fla…

Driveby: there's precedent for `optional` params defaulting to `null` in existing IDL, but not `undefined`.

I don't know for absolute certain whether or not `undefined` would compile, but maybe stick with `null` for consistency? `ScriptValuee::IsNull()` would then be the thing to check.

Ugh, so I'm (re-)learning that we can't use ` = undefined` as a default value in WebIDL, since it's used as the type, not the value.

So in that case, my recommendation is to change the overload that currently passes in `ScriptValue()` to instead pass in `ScriptValue(v8::Undefined(isolate))` (or whatever the right incantation is; `ScriptValue::CreateUndefined()` unfortunately doesn't exist yet), and CHECK that `IsEmpty()` is never true in our conversion function. Then we just have to handle the `IsUndefined()` case as a fallback to `{}`.

> I don't know for absolute certain whether or not undefined would compile, but maybe stick with null for consistency? ScriptValuee::IsNull() would then be the thing to check.

I'd rather just not have a default value, if we can't default to `{}` or `undefined`. We have to handle both of those cases explicitly already, so having a third value and forcing it to behave like `{}` is just a little more work in C++ world. I think the easiest thing is to just pass in an "undefined" ScriptValue from the overload that doesn't consume any `inputObject` from the bindings.

That way, everything converges down to two types, and we don't have to deal with a third default value.

Is it possible for source to kBroker and destination to be kNonBroker, yet the remote process is untrusted?

Also do we need to consider elevation here?

Yes: browser->renderer transports are {kBroker, kNonBroker} and untrusted, since renderers are launched with MOJO_SEND_INVITATION_FLAG_UNTRUSTED_PROCESS. Allowing it there is intentional, because mojo::DirectReceiver in renderers relies on is_same_remote_process to introduce an in-process node to the broker.

It's safe because the broker won't adopt kRecipient handles from an untrusted non-broker (`CanAcceptReceiverOwnedHandles()` requires peer trust). So the only processes that can end up here are the broker's own handle to that peer (is_same_remote_process), or a handle the peer itself held, duplicated out of the peer as kSender. Neither gives the peer anything beyond what it already has.

You mean ancestors outside a size container are not updated as part of the interleaved style recalc from laying out the container?

Is it that we somehow skip UpdateFirstLetterPseudoElement() in RecalcStyleForTraversalRootAncestor()?

Yes. `StyleEngine::RecalcStyle()` skips `RecalcStyleForTraversalRootAncestor()`
for the container's ancestors during interleaved style recalc, so they rely on
`RebuildLayoutTreeForSizeContainerAncestor()` during layout tree rebuild
instead. Removing the inner `::first-letter` can clear the rebuild root, so
that rebuild may not happen. Marking for rebuild makes sure it does.
